knowledge:
- key_parameters: prob=TRUE ;; prob=FALSE
- alternatives: impute.knn from the impute package for missing value imputation
- when_to_use: When classifying pediatric brain tumor samples into subtypes using DNA methylation beta values from Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation 450 BeadChip arrays.
- pitfalls: MethPed cannot be applied to datasets with missing values; checkNA must be used to identify missing values, and they must be imputed before classification. A large number of missing predictor probes (checked via probeMis) can drop predictive accuracy.

workflows.name: pediatric_tumor_classification
workflows.intent: Classify pediatric brain tumor samples into subtypes using DNA methylation beta values, handling potential missing values.
input: methylation_data.csv (matrix, data.frame, or ExpressionSet of DNA methylation beta values from Illumina 450k arrays)
workflows.stages: 1. Check for missing values in the input data using checkNA ;; 2. Impute missing values using impute.knn if necessary ;; 3. Run the MethPed classifier to obtain subtype probabilities or binary classifications ;; 4. Check for missing predictor probes using probeMis ;; 5. Summarize and visualize classification results using summary and plot
workflows.code:
library(MethPed)
data(MethPed_sample)
missingIndex <- checkNA(MethPed_sample)
myClassification <- MethPed(MethPed_sample)
myClassification
myClassification$target_id
myClassification$probes
myClassification$sample
myClassification$probes_missing
myClassification$oob_err.rate
myClassification$predictions
summary(myClassification)
myClassification_max <- MethPed(MethPed_sample,prob=FALSE)
summary(myClassification_max)
plot(myClassification)
probeMis(myClassification)
checkNA(MethPed_sample_missing)
if(exists(".Random.seed")) rm(.Random.seed)
library(impute)
imputedData <- impute.knn(MethPed_sample_missing)
imputedData <- imputedData$data
checkNA(imputedData)
myClassification <- MethPed(imputedData)
summary(myClassification)
